analysis.title: Liquid Insight: US FI supply: narrative flip in '27
key_insights: BofA estimates high-quality US fixed income supply (Treasuries, agency MBS, IG corporates) will be lower in 2027 than in 2026 on both a net and a 10-year-duration-adjusted basis. The report calls this a narrative flip.

Three drivers of the lower supply: Treasury relies more on bills than coupons, agency MBS supply slows with higher rates and less hedging flow, and IG issuance cools from the strong 2026 pace as bank and M&A issuance normalizes.

Using an old Fed QE rule of thumb (purchases equal to 1% of GDP in 10-year-equivalent duration lower the 10-year yield by about 10bp), the supply drop implies a 10-year Treasury yield about 12bp lower in 2027.
Treasury supply alone implies virtually no change in the 10-year yield. The -12bp effect comes from including IG and MBS supply. BofA says the 10-year impact is rough and highly uncertain.

BofA expects bills to reach 23.8% of marketable debt by the end of FY27 and 25.3% in FY28. A higher bill share that lets weighted average maturity shorten adds less fixed income duration to the market.

UST 2027 net supply declines because larger coupon maturities are refunded with bills and Treasury continues upsized buybacks funded with bills. The estimate assumes coupon size growth starts in Nov 2027, after the debt limit is resolved.

Agency MBS net issuance is projected at $167bn in 2027 versus $206bn in 2026, as high mortgage rates constrain housing activity. The 2H26 selloff added 2026 duration supply through convexity hedging, and stable to lower rates in 2027 should reduce it.
US IG gross supply is projected at $1.9tn in 2027 versus $2.1tn in 2026, with unusually heavy bank and M&A issuance normalizing and some issuance shifting to EUR on potentially cheaper funding.

AI-related bond supply is expected to be roughly stable in 2027 excluding GPU funding deals. Hyperscaler capex is higher, but pre-funding in 2026, equity raises, vendor financing and bank loans offset it.
BofA's TMT analyst expects big-5 hyperscaler bond issuance of $260bn across currencies in 2027 versus $300bn year to date in 2026. Including vendor financing, issuance would be flat year over year.

GPU funding deals are the wild card. They are generally privately placed in tranches with different credit risk, and some debt may go to private credit. BofA assumes about half of GPU funding competes directly with other IG supply.

Market implications, all else equal: less upward pressure on rates, which supports BofA's below-market end-2027 UST 10Y forecast of 4.75%. Wider US 30Y asset swap spreads are consistent with BofA's long 30Y ASW view. MBS and IG spread tightening is a tailwind.
Caveats: the MBS estimate covers agency only, the IG estimate excludes large privately placed GPU funding deals, and the 10-year impact is a rough rule of thumb.
Earlier BofA analysis put the impact of 2026's heavy high-quality supply on rates at about 30bp. BofA calls that number overly precise and only a ballpark.

trade_ideas.description: Long US 30Y asset swap spread. Latest -65bp, entry -71bp, target -55bp, stop -80bp.
trade_ideas.rationale: Lower net and duration-adjusted high-quality supply in 2027 supports wider (less negative) US asset swap spreads.

risk_factors: Higher future bill issuance is the stated risk to the long 30Y ASW trade.
GPU funding deals, mostly privately placed, could add IG-competing supply and offset the expected decline.
The 10-year impact estimate rests on a QE rule of thumb that may not be symmetric for supply, and carries a very high degree of uncertainty.
Wide range of outcomes for AI-related bond issuance.
The MBS estimate is agency only and the IG estimate excludes large privately placed GPU deals.
charts_described: Exhibit 5 table of 10Y-equivalent core bond duration supply ($bn): 2026 est total 4,894 (UST 2,670, MBS 551, IG 1,673) and 2027 est total 4,465 (UST 2,668, MBS 257, IG 1,540). Implied total core bond supply impact on 10Y rates is +28bp for 2026 and -12bp for 2027.
vol_and_positioning: The 2H26 rate selloff produced substantial MBS duration extension and convexity hedging, which added to 2026 duration supply. BofA expects less of this in 2027 if rates stabilize and gradually fall.
Rates are expected to stabilize and gradually drop in 2027, which reduces convexity-driven duration supply from MBS.
